items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to tire safety
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S2961

SPONSOR: KAPLAN
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to tire safety

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To improve public and highway safety

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

The bill would prohibit motor vehicle repair shops from repairing any
tire which would fail to meet Department of Motor Vehicle tire standards
after the completion of the repair.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

This legislation would prohibit a tire repair from being made to a tire
that would not meet Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) standards for the
use of tires by vehicles operated in New York State. Improper tire
repairs pose a safety risk to motorists. Repairing a tire that would not
meet DMV standards for passing a New York State motor vehicle inspection
would greatly increase the risk of tire failure.  Improperly repaired
tires can fail while in service, which may result in a vehicle crash and
cause serious personal injury or death.

A tire will fail a New York State motor vehicle inspection if the tread
is worn to less than 2/32 of an inch, the tire has a fabric break or a
cut in excess of one inch in any direction and is deep enough to reach
the body cords, the tire has visible bumps, bulges or knows, the tire
has any portion of the ply or cord structure exposed or the tire is
marked for specific non-highway uses. In any case, a tire will only fail
an inspection if it is a badly damaged tire that should not be driven on
for safety reasons. If a person attempts to repair a tire that would not
pass inspection, it is in the best interest of public safety to not
allow a tire repair to be performed.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2014: A7143
2016: A039A
2018: A8983

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the ninetieth day after it shall have
become a law

BILL NUMBER: S2961A

SPONSOR: KAPLAN
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in
relation to the repair of tires

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To ensure that motor vehicle repair shops shall not repair a tire under
certain enumerated conditions.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 adds a new subdivision 8 of Section 398-d of the vehicle and
traffic law to prohibit a vehicle repair shop to repair a tire if the
tire has exposed ply or cord, a bulge, knot or separation in either
sidewall or tread area. If tread wear indicators flush with the tread
outer surface in any two or more adjacent tread grooves.  Further, this
section prevents liability for a repair shot that makes a reasonable and
good faith determination that the tire upon repair would comply with
this section.

Section 2 is the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

This legislation would prohibit a tire repair from being made to a tire
that would not meet enumerated standards for which a tire would not pass
Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) standards for the use of tires by
vehicles operated in New York State. Improper tire repairs pose a safety
risk to motorists. Repairing a tire that would not meet DMV standards
for passing a New York State motor vehicle inspection would greatly
increase the risk of tire failure. Improperly repaired tires can fail
while in service, which may result in a vehicle crash and cause serious
personal injury or death.

A tire will fail a New York State motor vehicle inspection if the tread
is worn to less than 2/32 of an inch, the tire has a fabric break or a
cut in excess of one inch in any direction and is deep enough to reach
the body cords, the tire has visible bumps, bulges or knows, the tire
has any portion of the ply or cord structure exposed or the tire is
marked for specific non-highway uses. In any case, a tire will only fail
an inspection if it is a badly damaged tire that should not be driven on
for safety reasons. If a person attempts to repair a tire that  would
not pass inspection, it is in the best interest of public safety to not
allow a tire repair to be performed.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2014: A7143
2016: A039A
2018: A8983

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the ninetieth day after it shall.have
become a law
